title: Preventing Self-Siphonage: Trap Arm Length Rules
description: A trap arm is the section of pipe extending from the P-trap seal to its protective vent line connection. If a trap arm is installed too short or pitched too steeply, liquid flowing through can completely fill the pipe's cross-section, creating a siphonic action that sucks the protective water seal out of the trap. Without this water barrier, sewer gas freely enters the building. Plumbing codes dictate a minimum trap arm length—typically twice the pipe's internal diameter—to preserve atmospheric pressure balance and maintain a safe water seal every time the fixture drains.

Preventing Self-Siphonage: Trap Arm Length Rules

A trap arm is the section of pipe extending from the P-trap seal to its protective vent line connection. If a trap arm is installed too short or pitched too steeply, liquid flowing through can completely fill the pipe's cross-section, creating a siphonic action that sucks the protective water seal out of the trap. Without this water barrier, sewer gas freely enters the building. Plumbing codes dictate a minimum trap arm length—typically twice the pipe's internal diameter—to preserve atmospheric pressure balance and maintain a safe water seal every time the fixture drains.
